_doc: Plain-oracle witness for CrossCovenantRef (hash256 preimage + substr/bin2num).
This fixture needs NO signature and NO transaction context: the contract
hashes a caller-supplied byte string and compares it against a constructor-
baked hash256, then substrs a field out of it. So the differential oracle
(ANF interpreter vs the @bsv/sdk-backed ScriptVM, fold-ON bytes) can execute
it directly — which is why the previous `crypto-exempt.json` entry, whose own
reason admitted 'it likely COULD be witnessed ... but nobody has written that
spec yet', has been dropped in favour of this file.
Witness construction (all values below are derived, not arbitrary):
referencedOutput = e803000000000000  (8-byte LE amount = 1000 sats)
+ 22                (varint script length = 34)
+ 6a20              (OP_RETURN, PUSH 32)
+ 11 * 32           (the 32-byte state root)
sourceScriptHash = hash256(referencedOutput)
= b62b8750350efa7d279d2de817ee4a09aa2aabcf6bb3a64b5ad6a53d68c84e4e
stateRoot lives at byte offset 11, so substr(output, 11, 32) == 11*32.
bin2num(substr(output, 0, 8)) == 1000 (the LE amount field).
Both rejecting shapes are covered per method: a tampered preimage (fails the
hash256 equality) and a correct preimage with a wrong extracted value (passes
the hash check, fails the field assert) — so the hash guard and the extract
guard are each independently proven to be load-bearing.

spends.note: Authentic referenced output; state root at offset 11 matches.
First byte of the output flipped (e8 -> 17): hash256 != sourceScriptHash, so the authenticity guard must abort before any extraction.
Authentic output (hash guard passes) but the caller claims a state root of 22*32; the substr equality must abort. Proves the extract assert is load-bearing independently of the hash assert.
bin2num of the 8-byte LE amount field == 1000.
Authentic output, but the claimed numeric value is off by one; the bin2num equality must abort.
